title: Fleeting Inspiration
body:
On his This is It tour, Michael Jackson was asked by his director Kenny Ortega to tone down the constant additions to his set and production. 

Michael said "God channels this through me at night. I can't sleep because I'm so supercharged" 

Ortega jokingly replied: "Can't God take a vacation?"

To which Michael said: "You don't understand -- if I'm not there to receive these ideas, God might give them to Prince."

This idea wasn't held by MJ alone. Rick Rubin writes in The Creative Act: "If you have an idea you're excited about and you don't bring it to life, it it's not uncommon for the idea to find it's voice through another maker. This isn't because the other artist stole your idea, but because the idea's time has come."

When inspiration comes, it must be acted upon immediately, lest it find it's place in the mind of another.

title: Intentional Consumption
body:
In order to make fois gras, the ducks or geese undergo a process called gavage. It is a period of intense force feeding where a tube is stuck into the avian's mouth and they are forced to eat a high-fat mixture of corn and soy. This causes their livers to swell to ten times their natural size.

The problem with short-form content isn't that it punishes nuance, rewards controversy, shortens attention span, it is that you have no choice in what you consume. 

When I go on Youtube and see a mass of titles and thumbnails, none of which are interesting to me, you know what I do? I close my browser tab and go work on something productive. When I'm scrolling Instagram and I come across a reel I don't like, I just swipe to the next. 

Only a sick man would eat the same terrible meal over and over again in the hopes that it would one day taste good.
